title: How does a language model process text?
subtitle: Language models break text into small pieces called tokens before processing it mathematically.

intro.body: A token is a piece of text a model processes. It can be a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, or another text piece.
intro.metaphorLabel: A word-block metaphor, not real tokenizer boundaries
intro.metaphorNote: These word blocks are only a helpful picture of text pieces. Next, the real tokenizer may split them differently.

demo.body: Watch the verified Qwen2.5 tokenizer split the sentence into eight real token pieces.
demo.model: This example uses the Qwen2.5 tokenizer.
demo.different: Different models may split the same text differently.
demo.whyTitle: Why did it split this way?
demo.whyVocabulary: The tokenizer uses a fixed collection of text pieces.
demo.whyCommon: A familiar piece may stay together. A longer or less familiar word may be split into smaller pieces.

tokens.spaceLegend: means this token begins with a space.

correct.piece: Correct. A token is a piece of text the model processes. It may be a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, or another text piece.

incorrect.paragraph: A paragraph can contain many tokens. A token is a smaller text piece.
incorrect.word: Tokens are not always complete words. A word can be split into several tokens.
incorrect.picture: A token represents a text piece here, not a stored picture.
